reader.original: injn itoca itech qujça xochitl, ioan tlapalli

reader.translation: Its name comes from 'flower' and 'pigment/color' (explanation of xochipalli).
reader.notes: Book 11, folio 217r, Anderson–Dibble Nahuatl transcription. This short phrase derives the name xochipalli from xōchitl and tlapalli. 'Itoca' is the possessed 'name' form of the already listed noun tocaitl, not a new headword. The normalized vocalic lengths are editorial.

1.grammar: Possessed form of tocaitl, with 3sg possessor
1.notes: Cited on Book 11, folio 217r. Also listed in ODN tocaitl. A manual lexical link does not imply any new paradigm.

reader.title: Cantares Mexicanos · We go, we perish
reader.translation: We go away for good; we perish (poetic reading, approximate).
reader.notes: Cantares Mexicanos, f. 35r, as transcribed in Miguel León-Portilla, La filosofía náhuatl estudiada en sus fuentes (UNAM, 2017), p. 408, item 53. This is a secondary printed transcription, not a new check of the manuscript. Subject ti- is interpreted collectively from context, although ti- can also index 2sg. The line is poetry, not an isolated prose grammar example.

reader.title: Florentine Codex XI · Stone becomes a mirror
reader.original: in mochioa tezcatl, in mocuepa ca tetl
reader.normalized: in mochīhua tēzcatl in mocuepa ca tetl
reader.translation: Stone from which a mirror is made; a stone transformed into a mirror (descriptive excerpt).
reader.notes: Florentine Codex, Book 11, folio 209v, fifth section on stone used to make mirrors; Anderson–Dibble Nahuatl transcription. The original spelling, including 'mochioa', is reproduced in a short quoted fragment. 'Mochīhua' is a normalized editorial reading of reflexive/passive chīhua ('is made'); the particle ca is contextually ambiguous, not confidently translated as an isolated 'because'. Reflection and ritual divination are historically associated with polished mineral mirrors, but THIS clause itself does not claim that a stone literally sees hidden truths or the essence of nature.

1.grammar: Nonactive/reflexive form of chīhua, reading provisional
1.notes: The original transcription is 'mochioa'; normalized as mochīhua. Lexical relation to chīhua is sound, but exact voice and clause boundaries need separate grammatical review.
1.locator: Book 11, fol. 209v; section 5 on mirror stones

4.notes: Documented written form in folio 209v; do not generate additional verb conjugations from this line.

5.grammar: Emphatic/connective particle, or homographic verbal form; unresolved
